root_cause.text: The CAAM driver used kmemdup with `aligned_len` (rounded up for DMA cache alignment) instead of the actual key length `keylen`, causing an out-of-bounds read from the source key buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states “The copying is performed using kmemdup, however this leads to an overflow: reading more bytes (aligned_len - keylen) from the keylen source buffer.” The patch replaces `kmemdup(key, aligned_len, GFP_KERNEL)` with `kmalloc(aligned_len, GFP_KERNEL)` followed by `memcpy(hashed_key, key, keylen)`, which limits the copy to the actual key length.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential buffer overread in ahash_setkey by copying only the actual key length instead of aligned length.
intent_record.what: Replaced kmemdup(key, aligned_len, GFP_KERNEL) with kmalloc(aligned_len, GFP_KERNEL) plus memcpy(hashed_key, key, keylen), changing the copy length from aligned_len to keylen.
intent_record.how: The function now allocates a buffer of aligned_len bytes but copies only the actual key length (keylen) into it, preventing a buffer overread of the key source and ensuring the digest is computed from the intended key bytes.
